title: An unmanaged install can take a target namespace: the copy is re-namespaced at install through the duplicate-package rename engine
body:
epic:#3600#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPXwX1YfHyKJUh4agu

Filing-gate category: ② maintainer-directed task. Maintainer, verbatim (Claude Code session, 2026-11-06): 「有没有可能在安装的时候加上前缀，避免重复？」, then, on the seat's assessment and its default-namespace proposal: 「同意，裸名的问题立决策卡」. Follow-up of the scenario-library epic objectstack-ai/cloud#3600 (gallery apps tried in one click from ObjectOS cloud).

## Problem (customer-visible)

A customer who installs a starter template as their own copy (unmanaged) gets the template author's namespace forever: object names are identities and are never renamed after install (ADR-0129). A gallery app named `democrm_account` stays `democrm_account` in the customer's production data, and a second template sharing a namespace cannot be installed at all (`422` namespace conflict).

## Readings (origin/main 802c98cf)

- **The rename engine already exists.** `duplicatePackage` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts:122` onward) takes `targetNamespace` and re-namespaces a stored package: object renames with whole-identifier matching on both sides, bare names rewritten only at object-reference properties (the derived index `packages/metadata-protocol/src/reference-sites.ts`), record-key renames (`permission.objects`), view item names `<object>.<key>` and whole-value `target`s, refused collisions (never merged, never an invented name), and a prefix swap for non-object items that carry the source prefix. It carries fixes #19417, #19577, #23510, #24547 and the objectql `protocol-duplicate-package-*` test battery.
- **The unmanaged import keeps the source namespace.** `planUnmanagedImport` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.ts:435-485`) sets the base's namespace to the source's, per ruling Q3 = A on #15213 ("source namespace kept"; its reason was that copying into an existing base breaks that base's namespace on export, not a ban on renaming).
- **ADR-0048 §3.5** records rename-on-install as deferred future work; this card is that work.

## Ask

1. **One engine, two callers.** Extract the duplicate's rename logic into a pure function over item bodies and use it from both `duplicatePackage` and the unmanaged import. ⛔ No second copy of the logic.
2. **`targetNamespace` on the unmanaged import and the install-local door** (`MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin`), optional; absent keeps today's behaviour (source namespace). Validated by `ManifestSchema.shape.namespace`; reserved namespaces refused.
3. Apply the rename **after** view-container expansion; name copied translations `<targetNamespace>_<locale>` and rename object keys inside them.
4. Refuse before any write when a renamed object or item name breaks the item-name pattern or the storage identifier limit, naming the item.
5. Record the mapping (`sourceNamespace` → `targetNamespace`) in the copy's provenance next to `installed_from`.
6. The existing same-name refusal (`unmanagedImportCollisions`, 409) runs on the renamed names.
7. **Q6 on #15213 stands**: a later managed install of the same source package stays refused (seat default; the maintainer may reopen).
8. Amend ADR-0048 §3.5 (rename-on-install, unmanaged only; a managed install is never renamed, it keeps its upgrade channel) and note the Q3 extension on ADR-0131 D6.
9. **Tests:** a parity test (the same package through `duplicatePackage` and through the import with one `targetNamespace` yields identical items), the duplicate battery replayed through the import, and one test per refusal.

Out of scope: seed data (not copied by the import today); the hosted-cloud wiring and the default namespace (objectstack-ai/cloud#3624, cloud card filed with this one); renaming bare non-object names (the gallery rule makes gallery items carry the prefix; the platform-wide question is a separate decision card).

Reader: the `domain:engine` lane seat, from `pm:queue`.
